title: Read an attribute
summary: An attribute is an extra fact written in a tag.
introduction: An attribute is an extra fact written in a tag. Your task: Remove name and check the fallback greeting.
learningObjectives: Remove name and check the fallback greeting.
Explain the example for read an attribute

blocks.text: An attribute is an extra fact written in a tag. A custom element can read it with getAttribute.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<reader-name name="Mia"></reader-name>
<script>
  class ReaderName extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.textContent = "Hi, " + (this.getAttribute("name") || "reader"); }
  }
  customElements.define("reader-name", ReaderName);
</script>
blocks.title: Read an attribute

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`connectedCallback` runs when the element joins the document. It can run again after a removal and reconnection.

blocks.text: The tag shows Hi, Mia. Without the name attribute, it uses reader.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: getAttribute returns text or null. Choose a fallback for a missing attribute.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Remove name and check the fallback greeting.
